parts.title: The clustering of IT companies
parts.article:
The clustering of IT companies

A Alfred Marshall, one of the fathers of modern economics, was asked why firms in the same industry were often geographically located near each other. Proximity, he replied, created something ‘in the air’. He went on to explain, ‘If one man starts a new idea, it is taken up by others and combined with suggestions of their own, and thus it becomes a source of further new ideas.’ Marshall was thinking about traditional 19th-century manufacturing companies, but the same is true of IT companies of the 21st century. Silicon Valley, an area near San Francisco in the USA, is home to many of the industry’s giants, and hopeful founders of young start-up companies still head there.

B Economic theory suggests several main reasons why historically firms from the same industry—for example, steel makers or clothing manufacturers—have ended up in the same place. Some may depend on the availability of natural resources such as coal or being close to a harbour or river for shipping goods. A concentration of firms also creates a pool of specialized workers, and this benefits both employees and employers: the former are likely to find jobs and the latter are likely to find staff. Yet another reason is that subsidiary trades spring up to supply specialised inputs required by the primary industry. And inevitably, industries cluster together because ideas spill over from one firm to the next.

C But there are also forces that encourage companies to spread out. One is the cost of transporting products to widely dispersed customers. Another is that rents tend to rise when firms cluster together. You might imagine that the dramatic fall in the cost of computing would have pushed firms in the IT industry farther apart. Natural resources do not matter to them as they do to many traditional manufacturing industries, and the ease of online communication should reduce the need for staff to be close together to deal with customers and suppliers or to swap ideas. But none of this seems to count against Silicon Valley, where commercial property prices are high, and against other IT centres like London and New York, which are not only expensive, but also lack California’s high-tech history. There are plenty of other places in Europe where costs are lower, but they currently lack sufficient appeal.

D Although you can find high-tech companies of all shapes and sizes in these IT centres, the smaller ones especially have a fondness for clustering together. As Jed Kolko, an economist for an international property company, explains, the less an industry needs to be near its suppliers or its customers, the more likely it is to locate where the jobs are already, such as Silicon Valley, or in major cities like London or New York. In Russia, says one knowledgeable observer of the IT scene, for a university kid studying in the regions, moving to Moscow sounds smart.

E The area around Silicon Valley now has clusters inside clusters—that is, specific smaller geographic areas where similar IT companies are located. Within the borders of the Valley, makers of semiconductors and network equipment are found mostly around the city of San Jose, while search engine and social network companies are located farther to the north. Even in San Francisco there are divisions with similar companies located in specific city districts.

F Young IT companies need more than a workforce; they also need access to money and expert advice. If a company is located in a cluster with other IT companies, staff can have more face-to-face communication with like-minded people from other companies, which is often more productive than phone calls or emails. Also, there is a better chance of making contact with someone with money and an interest in potentially profitable ideas. Even in industries which are built around virtual relationships, physical contact can be invaluable. The recycling of people is important, too. As people move from company to company in Silicon Valley, and as one company buys or merges with another, a whole network of people who know each other develops, and these people are able to communicate easily with each other, and hire each other.

G In places like Silicon Valley, people are also close to the latest ideas. ‘New ideas become known in that tiny region perhaps years ahead of the rest of the world,’ argues one Valley entrepreneur. ‘You are always building on the idea that came immediately before. If you are trying to build the thing that comes next, being aware of information about innovations that are already out there helps you.’ This sounds very much like the point Marshall was trying to make.

H Will other IT hubs ever catch up with Silicon Valley? Berlin and perhaps some other international cities like Beijing have several things going for them. One is size: they are big and lively and act as magnets for young, creative people in search of opportunities. The other advantage of these cities is that many other types of industries are located there, and hence they offer various skills on which IT companies can draw. To many, this variety may prove invaluable.

questions.question: an example of geographic clustering of IT companies within a city

analyses.content: 段落E明确提到了旧金山（San Francisco）这个城市内部不同区域针对相似公司有具体的划分，直接对应题干中“一个城市内部（within a city）的地理聚集”。
你可能会只看第一句而误选A，但A段只提到了硅谷整体的聚集现象，并没有深入描述“单个城市内部”的具体分区。

The area around Silicon Valley now has clusters inside clusters—that is, specific smaller geographic areas where similar IT companies are located. Within the borders of the Valley, makers of semiconductors and network equipment are found mostly around the city of San Jose, while search engine and social network companies are located farther to the north. Even in San Francisco there are divisions with similar companies located in specific city districts.

questions.question: an argument that access to the latest thinking allows clustered IT companies to make further progress

analyses.content: 段落G指出，了解前沿的创新信息能帮你打造下一个新事物，直接对应题干“接触最新思维能让公司取得进一步发展（make further progress）”。
你可能会因为看到“new idea”而去选A段，但A段仅仅在讲新想法是如何产生的，而G段才真正强调了利用这些新想法去“取得进展（build the thing that comes next）”。

If you are trying to build the thing that comes next, being aware of information about innovations that are already out there helps you.’

questions.question: a reference to how employee preferences are considered by companies

analyses.content: 段落D通过大学生觉得“搬到莫斯科去显得很明智”这个具体例子，说明了公司在选址时会迎合员工喜欢去大城市的偏好（locate where the jobs are already）。
你可能会在H段纠结，虽然H段提到了城市吸引年轻人，但只有D段从“公司选址策略”的角度回应了公司是如何“考虑（considered）”员工偏好的。

In Russia, says one knowledgeable observer of the IT scene, for a university kid studying in the regions, moving to Moscow sounds smart.

questions.question: a reference to the views of an early economist

analyses.content: 段落A开篇就引用了现代经济学之父之一Alfred Marshall的观点，完美对应题干寻找的“早期（early）经济学家的观点”。
你可能会错选D，因为D段也有个经济学家（Jed Kolko），但他所在的国际房地产公司显然属于现代背景，不符合“早期”这个极其重要的限定词。

Proximity, he replied, created something ‘in the air’. He went on to explain, ‘If one man starts a new idea, it is taken up by others and combined with suggestions of their own, and thus it becomes a source of further new ideas.’

questions.question: a description of the appeal certain large cities may have for IT companies

analyses.content: 段落H详细列举了柏林、北京等大城市对IT公司的吸引力，包括规模大、充满活力以及能提供多样化的技能人才。
你可能会选C，虽然C段提到了纽约和伦敦，但它强调的是这些城市“虽然贵但依然有IT公司去”，而H段才是全面正面地“描述（description）”了大城市的具体吸引力优势。

Berlin and perhaps some other international cities like Beijing have several things going for them. One is size: they are big and lively and act as magnets for young, creative people in search of opportunities. The other advantage of these cities is that many other types of industries are located there, and hence they offer various skills on which IT companies can draw. To many, this variety may prove invaluable.

questions.question: several examples of why meeting people in person is important

analyses.content: 段落F明确列举了面对面交流（face-to-face/physical contact）的几个好处：沟通更高效、更容易遇到投资人等，直接对应题干。
你可能会因为找“沟通”去选C段的在线交流，但题目问的是“in person（亲自/面对面）”，所以必须锁定F段的“face-to-face”和“physical contact”。

Also, there is a better chance of making contact with someone with money and an interest in potentially profitable ideas. Even in industries which are built around virtual relationships, physical contact can be invaluable.

questions.question: The list below gives some possible reasons why traditional companies have clustered together. Which TWO of these reasons are mentioned by the writer of the text?

analyses.content: B段明确提到，公司聚集会创造出一个“专业工人池（pool of specialized workers）”，这直接等同于选项A的“熟练劳动力市场（skilled labour market）”。
你可能会凭借自己的生活常识去选B（学术中心），觉得IT公司肯定靠近大学，但B段讲传统公司时原文压根没有任何关于学术（academic）的词汇。
A concentration of firms also creates a pool of specialized workers, and this benefits both employees and employers: the former are likely to find jobs and the latter are likely to find staff.

questions.question: The list below gives some possible reasons why traditional companies have clustered together. Which TWO of these reasons are mentioned by the writer of the text?

analyses.content: B段指出传统公司选址依赖于“靠近港口或河流来运输货物”，这完美转述了选项E的“水上交通（water transport）”。
你可能会看到原文的“natural resources（煤炭等自然资源）”就想在选项里找，千万别把它和C选项的“favourable climate（好气候）”强行凑对，原文根本没提气候。
Some may depend on the availability of natural resources such as coal or being close to a harbour or river for shipping goods.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following cities does the writer say are attractive to IT workers despite cost there being high?

analyses.content: C段明确指出，伦敦（London）是一个不但生活成本昂贵（expensive），而且缺乏加州那种高科技历史背景，却依然对IT公司有吸引力的地方。
你可能会去选D或者E（柏林或北京），但它们出现在H段时，原文并没有给它们加上“成本高昂（cost being high）”这个前提限制条件。

But none of this seems to count against Silicon Valley, where commercial property prices are high, and against other IT centres like London and New York, which are not only expensive, but also lack California’s high-tech history.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following cities does the writer say are attractive to IT workers despite cost there being high?

analyses.content: 纽约（New York）同样被C段点名为生活成本高（expensive）但公司依然扎堆的城市。
你可能会因为在D段看到了莫斯科（Moscow）而选C，但莫斯科的例子是为了说明年轻人的偏好，通篇没有提到莫斯科“生活成本高”。

But none of this seems to count against Silicon Valley, where commercial property prices are high, and against other IT centres like London and New York, which are not only expensive, but also lack California’s high-tech history.

groups.contentHtml:
24 Some IT centres like Berlin and Beijing have an advantage of .
25 They have the ability to attract talent and provide , as well as jobs, for ambitious young people.
26 The workforce in such international cities also offers a wide range of for the companies located there to make use of.

analyses.content: H段讲到柏林和北京有几个优势时，直接冒号引出的第一个优势就是它们的“规模（size）”。
你可能会想填magnets（磁铁），但注意题干结构是“have an advantage of...（拥有...的优势）”，对应原文“One is size”，这里需要填的是核心名词优势本身。

Berlin and perhaps some other international cities like Beijing have several things going for them. One is size: they are big and lively and act as magnets for young, creative people in search of opportunities.
原文H段提到这些大城市像磁铁一样吸引着寻找“机会（opportunities）”的年轻且富有创造力的人才，直接对应填空。
你极容易顺手填jobs（工作），但题干里已经明确写了“as well as jobs”，再填jobs就语义重复了，必须回原文找除了工作之外年轻人还在寻找什么。
One is size: they are big and lively and act as magnets for young, creative people in search of opportunities.
H段说明，因为这些城市还有很多其他产业，所以这批劳动力能提供各种各样的“技能（skills）”供IT公司去利用（draw on / make use of）。
你可能会填industries（产业），但请结合题干逻辑：是城市的劳动力（workforce）能为公司提供什么，劳动力提供的只能是“技能”，而不是提供产业。

The other advantage of these cities is that many other types of industries are located there, and hence they offer various skills on which IT companies can draw. To many, this variety may prove invaluable.
